subject: Capacity pressure: sustained reserved throughput degradation — stakeholder rally
messages:
From: Emily Tran <emily.tran@finexa.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Finexa ProdOps <prodops@finexa.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Strange throughput/500 spike on our reserved pool — urgent

Mina —

We started seeing a sustained increase in 5xx errors and token-level queueing on our reserved pool at ~08:40 PST. Latency p95 is up ~3x, and our throttling counter shows sustained headroom exhaustion. This is impacting our real-time credit decisioning flow. Screenshots attached.

Can Redwood confirm whether this is a capacity or runtime regression? We are now seeing errors on live traffic (500/502) that weren’t present earlier. We need an ETA for mitigation — our merchants are already affected.

—Emily
Emily Tran
Head of Platform, Finexa

Attachments: finexa_error_snapshot_20280311.png
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Tran <emily.tran@finexa.com>, Finexa ProdOps <prodops@finexa.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Mar 2028 09:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Strange throughput/500 spike on our reserved pool — urgent

Emily — thank you for the signal and the screenshots. We're on it. Quick summary of what we see on our side:

- Metrics (live): reserved pool rsv-prod-finexa-01 shows sustained CPU/GPU slot saturation since 08:35 PST; autoscaler did not provision additional capacity due to an aggressive headroom guard.
- Error pattern: elevated kernel OOM/gateway 502 wave correlated with longer KV cache miss rates.
- Immediate ask: can Finexa switch a small percentage (5–10%) of traffic to the hosted fallback endpoint for the next 30–60 minutes? That would reduce pressure and buy time for remediation.

I'm looping Marcus and Irene to own remediation and to propose short-term mitigations. We'll share a concrete MAP in 30 minutes.

—Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Emily Tran <emily.tran@finexa.com>, Finexa ProdOps <prodops@finexa.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Mar 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Strange throughput/500 spike on our reserved pool — urgent

Team — quick technical readout (observability snippets attached):

- Root hypothesis: sudden workload skew (longer sequences + more streaming requests) pushed rsv-prod-finexa-01 into continuous batching with KV eviction thrash. The runtime's guardrail prevented new GPUs from attaching because recent autoscale policy threshold was hit and the policy uses a conservative cooldown.
- Repro attempt: replicated a micro-burst using Finexa traffic profile; saw the same p95 jump and 502 spike after 2 minutes.

Immediate actions I recommend now:
1) Toggle temporary policy override to allow 30% burst capacity for the next 90 minutes (ops).
2) Enable model-variant fallback for Finexa route to a lightly-quantized compatible variant to reduce memory pressure (runtime).
3) Request Finexa to divert 7% of traffic to hosted fallback (per Mina's note).

Irene and I will implement (1) and (2) now. I'll monitor and report back in 20 minutes with impact metrics and whether the error rate drops.

Attachments: realtime_metrics_logs_20280311.tar.gz

—Marcus
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Mar 2028 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec sync: Finexa reserved throughput shortfall — request for stakeholder rally

Folks —

After the quick interventions Marcus put in place we saw partial recovery: p95 latency reduced ~30% and 5xx rate fell but remained above Finexa's SLA threshold (current 5xx ~1.9% vs SLA 0.5%). Finexa has asked for an executive-level commitment and a clear MAP that includes timeline to full remediation.

Proposed agenda for a stakeholder rally (today, within 3 hrs):
- Live readout (Marcus) with metrics and what we changed
- Risk analysis: autoscaler policy, kernel regressions, model variant memory profile (Irene)
- Customer impact and mitigation timeline (mine)
- Asks for execs: temporary capacity reservation (commit + billing terms), priority dev resources for deterministic regression (Jonas), and sales-approved customer credits if SLA breach persists (Marissa).

Please confirm availability for a 30-minute huddle today between 15:00–16:00 PST. We need an exec anchor in the call (CTO/Head of Infra) — Jonas, can you escalate for coverage? Marissa — please prepare a short credit/contract options pack we can present to Finexa if needed.

—Mina
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Emily Tran <emily.tran@finexa.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Exec sync: Finexa reserved throughput shortfall — request for stakeholder rally

Mina / team / Emily —

Thanks for the clear notes. I secured CTO coverage for a 15:30 PST rally today and asked Infra to prepare two concrete proposals:

A) Short-term: Emergency reserved capacity top-up — provision up to 40% extra GPUs to Finexa's pool for 6 hours. Billing to be handled as a committed short-term addendum (we will draft language). Operationally this will be available within ~25 minutes of approval.

B) Mid-term (3–5 days): Root-cause sprint led by Infra + Runtime to confirm whether this was a policy/config regression or a workload shift; deliverables: autoscaler patch (allow faster burst), kernel memory-stability patch, and a model-variant rollout plan with canarying.

Jonas (on call) will present A/B, Marissa will have draft credit scenarios ready (Marissa: pls confirm). Marcus/Irene — please bring the post-change metrics and a short runbook for the emergency top-up so we can perform the action immediately if Finexa agrees.

Emily — we will join the 15:30 PST call; thanks for your patience, we realize the impact and are treating this as priority.

—Jonas Weber
Head of Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
